spoken_script.narration_text: So a tokenized money-market fund just means the fund gives you a token instead of a line in a spreadsheet? That's the mechanism, but the token isn't the interesting part. The interesting part is who can create or destroy that token. Isn't that just the fund company, same as before? Usually yes, and that's exactly the catch. The speed of the token makes settlement feel instant, but the person who controls redemption hasn't actually changed. So if everyone tries to cash out at once? Then you're back to the same limit the underlying market has always had, a repo market that can't deliver cash instantly. The token never removed that limit, it just made it easier to forget it exists.
